newsitem.title: UK: Elton John wants to smell the roses on his 50th.
newsitem.headline: Elton John wants to smell the roses on his 50th.

text.p: Gone are the drugs, drinks and tantrums. Rock icon Elton John just wants to smell the roses on his 50th birthday.
The flamboyant showman, once addicted to cocaine and vodka martinis, is now "one happy budgie" who has come firmly out of the gay closet and turned his back on a killer lifestyle.

He now sports the rock world's most famous hair transplant and, like fellow pop veterans David Bowie and Mick Jagger, will not be growing old gracefully. Rocket Man has plenty of fuel still left -- even after selling 200 million records.
John once thought nothing of eating 20 pots of cockles, a popular shellfish snack, and a tub of ice cream before breakfast and then, in typical bulimic fashion, throwing it all up.
He was hooked on cocaine and washed it down with a bottle of whisky a night. An obsession with his ballooning weight led him to have lamb urine injections.
But after two decades of self-destructive madness, meeting young AIDS victim Ryan White gave John a sense of proportion that stopped him becoming yet another rock obituary.

John, who at the height of his fame in 1975 tried to kill himself with a bottle of valium, finally conquered his addictions, admitted his homosexuality and donated millions in royalties to AIDS research.
On Thursday he celebrates the half century that some thought he might never see and his AIDS Benefit Party looks set to be the hottest ticket in town on Hollywood Oscar night.

The self-styled "Queen Mother of Pop" is in reflective mood after surviving the sex, drugs and rock 'n roll rollercoaster, telling his biographer Philip Norman: "There are roses growing out there that I never had time to stop and smell.
"For the next few years, I just want to smell the roses."
He has at last found serenity, looks younger than he did in the swinging Sixties and even released a single with another slimmed-down superstar -- Luciano Pavarotti.
"I've had such blessings in my life, yet I used to make these awful scenes. I'll never complain again," he pledges.
But his latest venture -- a rock concert to mark Hong Kong's handover to China at the end of June -- failed to get off the ground because his sound system was above the stadium's decibel limit.

Like the chameleon Bowie, John has undergone many a metamorphosis since the 1970s when he swaggered on stage in jewelled spectacles, high heels and sequinned costumes. Now he even writes Oscar-winning songs for Disney cartoon films.
But the hunger to succeed is still there: "People say the music business is competitive -- and it is -- but I like the struggle to stay at the top. It keeps me going.
"I don't begrudge anyone else their success. Stevie Wonder can eat me for breakfast as far as musicianship goes, but that doesn't make me angry or paranoid."
